clue.text: Impair the spirit of the Border

parts.note: to impair something is to mar or spoil it
gin is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: Something that dampens the mood of the Scottish Borders region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Border' suggests the Anglo-Scottish Borders, but here it means an edge or rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the edge of a page or field is its border.

clue.text: Work of a struggling German artist

definitions.text: Work of a struggling German artist

parts.words: Work of a struggling German artist
parts.note: Hitler had tried to be a painter, and his book's title means 'my struggle'

explanation.surface: A painting by a German artist who cannot make ends meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' suggests poverty, but it points to the book's title, German for 'my struggle'; its author had once been a would-be artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler's book, written in prison in 1924, its title German for 'my struggle'.

clue.text: "In quiet she" (Arnold)

parts.note: a gap-fill from Matthew Arnold's poem Requiescat, whose line goes 'In quiet she ...'

explanation.surface: A quotation from Matthew Arnold with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold's Requiescat, about a dead woman: 'Her life was turning, turning ... But for peace her soul was yearning, And now peace laps her round ... In quiet she reposes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb completes Arnold's line, meaning she lies at rest.

clue.text: Brought in the odd reduction, about 500

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around, about, the number
an odd arrangement of reduction is one jumbled out of order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A strange price cut of around five hundred has been brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges REDUCTION, and 'about' puts it around D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something introduced has been brought in or presented.

clue.text: Con-man explains motive for the Klondike Rush

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose, a motive for acting
gold drove the Klondike Rush, and OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A swindler explains why prospectors rushed to the Yukon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con-man' is not a swindler: it is someone who is 'con', against, as in pro and con. The Klondike Rush was the 1890s gold rush in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues the 'con' side of a question is an opponent of it, one who protests.

clue.text: Including papers, this won't take long in court

definitions.text: Including papers, this won't take long in court

parts.words: Including papers, this won't take long in court
parts.note: a lawyer's case for papers, and also a legal hearing that is short

explanation.surface: A trial with documents that will be over quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is a short (brief) court case; as one it is a holder for documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat bag for carrying documents, and taken apart a short legal hearing.

clue.text: The player's out

parts.note: the stage direction marking an actor leaving the stage

explanation.surface: A sportsman has been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, where 'out' means dismissed, but it is an actor, and the Latin stage direction says he goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction meaning an actor leaves, and more generally a way out.

clue.text: To correspond in every respect

parts.note: to tally is to correspond or agree

explanation.surface: Matching up exactly in each detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something wholly so is so completely, in every way.

clue.text: Car mounting 'the roundabout is a fast one

definitions.text: Car mounting 'the roundabout is a fast one

parts.words: Car mounting 'the roundabout is a fast one
parts.note: car read upwards in a down clue, extended so the word reads the same both ways, as a roundabout brings you back, describing a fast car

explanation.surface: A vehicle driving over a traffic island must be speeding.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue CAR going up reads RAC, and the whole answer reads the same in both directions, like a trip round a roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast car built for competition.

clue.text: Deity that: sounds inactive

indicators.note: sounds says the word for inactive is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: inactive means idle

explanation.surface: A god that seems to do nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An image worshipped as a god, a false god.

clue.text: Ascribed to 'one sea being out of place

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the sea word stands outside, around, the word meaning place

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Something attributed to a single sea that has moved from where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out of' is a container signal: the sea word sits outside the word for place. 'Out of place' looks like an anagram signal, but nothing is scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quality imputed to someone is attributed or credited to them.

clue.text: Like Bumble's asinine law

parts.note: Mr Bumble in Dickens's Oliver Twist says the law is 'a ass, a idiot', so the law as he describes it is foolish

explanation.surface: Describing the foolish law that a Dickens character complains about.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bumble is the beadle in Oliver Twist; his famous line is 'the law is a ass — a idiot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumble calls the law an idiot, so the adjective for it means foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Romantic quickening?

parts.note: reviving someone by mouth-to-mouth breathing is pictured as a romantic act, a quickening being a bringing back to life

explanation.surface: A love affair that makes the heart beat faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickening' in its old sense means bringing to life; mouth-to-mouth resuscitation looks like a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-aid name for mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, which restores breathing and so revives a person.

clue.text: Of the wing to the French right

parts.note: in French 'to the' (feminine) is à la

explanation.surface: A phrase about the right wing of French politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective from Latin ala, wing, describes things relating to wings.

clue.text: For the surrender, a moving ceremony

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a cession is a surrender, the giving up of territory or rights

explanation.surface: Laying down arms is an emotional occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' suggests emotional, but the ceremony literally moves along.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade or march is a ceremony in which people move along in order.

clue.text: Disorder of old Christmas revels

explanation.surface: Chaos at Christmas parties in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord of Misrule presided over Christmas revelry in medieval and Tudor England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad government brings disorder, and the old festive season of topsy-turvy merrymaking was named after its mock ruler.

clue.text: Site Manet possibly used for The Absinthe Drinker ?

definitions.text: Site Manet possibly used for The Absinthe Drinker

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of site Manet may form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering where the painter set his picture of a man drinking absinthe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SITE MANET. Manet painted The Absinthe Drinker in 1859, and a small French café is just where such a drinker would sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French café selling drinks, the setting for an absinthe drinker.

clue.text: Dressed for a foray, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the phrase meaning a foray to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a foray is a raid, an attack into enemy territory

explanation.surface: Getting kitted out to go on a military raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be arrayed is to be clothed or decked out.

clue.text: Though Voltaire would call it encouragement of others

definitions.text: Though Voltaire would call it encouragement of others

parts.words: Though Voltaire would call it encouragement of others
parts.note: Voltaire wrote that Admiral Byng was shot 'pour encourager les autres', to encourage the others, meaning to frighten them into line

explanation.surface: A French writer's ironic view of something that motivates people.
explanation.walkthrough: In Candide Voltaire says the English shoot an admiral now and then 'to encourage the others'; the irony is that the execution discourages failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that discourages by fear, like an execution meant as a warning to others.

clue.text: Seizure includes F.B.I. types? That's made up!

indicators.note: the word for a seizure contains, takes in, the agents' nickname

parts.note: a fit is a seizure, a sudden attack
G-men is American slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: An attack involving federal agents turns out to be invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' is the container signal. G-men (government men) is 1930s American slang for FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment of the imagination is something invented, not real.

clue.text: Creation of a book ? Contrariwise

parts.note: turn the phrase round, a book of creation: the first book of the Bible tells the story of the Creation

explanation.surface: Asking how a book is written, then the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creation of a book' suggests writing one; 'contrariwise' says reverse it: the book of the Creation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's opening book, which narrates the creation of the world, and whose name means origin.

clue.text: Charm clueful Charlie into a complicated net

indicators.note: the detective's surname goes inside the rearranged net
a complicated net is one tangled up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Charlie Chan is the fictional detective, full of clues

explanation.surface: Enticing a clever man called Charlie into a tangled net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' scrambles the net, and 'into' puts the detective inside it. Charlie Chan was a Chinese-American detective in 1930s novels and films.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enchant someone is to charm or bewitch them.

clue.text: Movement is noted and the volcano goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue the volcano going up reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A tremor is recorded and the volcano erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' looks like an eruption, but in a down clue it reverses ETNA to ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of a symphony is often named by its tempo marking, here a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Stick this — it may do the trick

definitions.text: Stick this — it may do the trick

parts.words: Stick this — it may do the trick
parts.note: a magician's stick is the tool that performs the conjuring trick

explanation.surface: Advice to persevere, since the method might work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick this' looks like 'keep at it', but it describes a stick, and 'the trick' is a conjuring trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's rod, waved to make a trick happen.

clue.text: It keeps the fisherman's foot drier than its own

definitions.text: It keeps the fisherman's foot drier than its own

parts.words: It keeps the fisherman's foot drier than its own
parts.note: a long waterproof boot worn by anglers, and also a long-legged bird that stands in water with wet feet

explanation.surface: A boot that keeps an angler dry, unlike its namesake.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a fisherman's waterproof boot and a heron-like bird whose own feet stand in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A thigh-high waterproof boot, sharing its name with long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: A doctor as unhappy to get nothing right as a diplomat

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
unhappy means sad
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A doctor who is as gloomy as an envoy forced to accept no rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' looks like an anagram signal for 'as', but it is SAD, and the pieces line up as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is the senior envoy representing a country abroad.

clue.text: Put some coals on, too

indicators.note: some means only part of the words coals on is taken

explanation.surface: Instruction to add a few lumps of coal to the fire as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to letters inside 'coals on': cOALSo... the run A-L-S-O spans the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: also means in addition, as well.

clue.text: Gilpin's goal, Big Ben for instance

explanation.surface: Where a famous rider was heading, and a London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cowper's comic ballad John Gilpin, he means to dine at the Bell inn at Edmonton but his horse bolts past it. Big Ben is the great bell in the Westminster clock tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilpin's destination was an inn of that name, and Big Ben is the name of a large ringing chime in London.

clue.text: How does poor Cinders make out?

indicators.note: poor here signals Cinders in a sorry state, her letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking how Cinderella manages in her poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' looks like 'get on', but it means 'perceive'. 'poor' rearranges CINDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make out something faint is to perceive or detect it.

clue.text: Knowledge of truth or fiction

parts.note: organised knowledge of facts, which also names the genre of ... fiction

explanation.surface: Learning that might come from facts or from stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means systematic knowledge of what is true, yet it also heads the phrase for a genre of made-up stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin scientia, knowledge, and also prefixes 'fiction' for a literary genre.

clue.text: Determined to give wild rose to a music-maker

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of rose are running loose, rearranged

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument, a maker of music

explanation.surface: A suitor set on giving a wild rose to a minstrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the flower's letters; 'Determined' is the definition, an adjective, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a resolute person is firm and determined.

clue.text: Demonstrate "Bottoms Up" in green

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Showing a drinking toast while wearing green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms up' looks like a toast, but to show it literally is to turn something upside down. Vert is green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down puts its bottom on top.
